home.title: Nation Furnace — HVAC in Burnaby since 2003
home.description: Burnaby HVAC company. Furnaces, boilers, heat pumps, air conditioning, hot water and duct work for homes and commercial buildings. Open 8am to 8pm, seven days.
home.h1: Heating and cooling in Burnaby since 2003
home.lede: We install and repair furnaces, boilers, heat pumps, air conditioning and hot water systems in houses and commercial buildings across Burnaby.
intro: Dino Gerami started the company in Burnaby in 2003, and we've worked out of the same city ever since.

Burnaby housing isn't one thing. There are post-war houses where the heating has been rebuilt two or three times over, and there are towers going up around Metrotown and Brentwood that were designed around the equipment we fit new. A furnace swap in a 1950s basement usually means working around whatever ductwork the last few owners left behind. That's a different afternoon than a heat pump on a new build.
home.shotsIntro: Heating, cooling, hot water and ventilation, as service calls, repairs or full installs. The breakdown is on {{servicesLink}}.
home.commercial: Rooftop units, make-up air, and the heating plant in strata and light industrial buildings. Still Creek and the Lake City industrial area are close by, so a good share of the commercial work is within a few minutes of the shop.
home.contactIntro: The office is on Still Creek Drive. Someone answers the phone seven days a week between 8am and 8pm.

services.title: What we do — Nation Furnace, Burnaby
services.description: Furnaces, boilers, heat pumps, gas fireplaces, air conditioning, hot water and duct cleaning. Repairs and installs across Burnaby.
services.lede: Heating, cooling, hot water and ventilation. Any of it as a service call, a repair, or a full replacement.

groups.heading: Furnaces
body: The bulk of our winter. Ignition faults, blower motors, cracked heat exchangers, and the annual service that catches most of it before December. When a furnace is past saving we handle the swap, including whatever the old ductwork needs to make the new unit breathe properly.
We install Ducane, Coleman and Lennox equipment, among others. More on {{link:https://nationheating.ca/furnace|furnace work}}.
groups.caption: Panel off on a new install: blower, dual PVC flues, gas flex line.

groups.heading: Boilers
body: Hydronic systems, radiators and in-floor heat. Pressure loss, circulation pumps, controls that have drifted, and full replacements when a unit is finished. A good share of Burnaby heats with hot water rather than forced air, so there's {{featureLink}}.

groups.heading: Heat pumps
body: One unit that heats in winter and cools in summer, which is why they have taken off here. We install and service inverter mini-splits and ducted systems, and we'll tell you honestly whether your house suits one before you spend the money.

groups.heading: Air conditioning
body: Installs, seasonal start-ups and repairs. Try to book the service before the first real heat arrives rather than during it. The whole trade gets buried in the same week. See {{link:https://nationheating.ca/air-conditioning|air conditioning}}.

groups.heading: Gas fireplaces
body: Pilot and ignition faults, glass, log sets, and new inserts. Run a fireplace that has sat all summer once in the fall, before you need it. Better to find a dead pilot in October than in a cold snap.
groups.caption: Gas insert, ceramic logs, herringbone firebox.

groups.heading: Hot water
body: Tanks and tankless both. Tanks are usually thermostats, elements, sediment, or a leak that has been ignored for a while. Tankless units are happier on a service schedule than left alone until they quit.
We fit Navien and Noritz units regularly. More on {{link:https://nationheating.ca/tankless-water-heater|tankless water heaters}}.
groups.caption: Navien tankless, PEX runs and PVC venting.

groups.heading: Air ducts and dryer vents
body: Supply and return duct cleaning for houses and commercial units, and dryer vent cleaning. A restricted dryer vent shows up as longer drying times well before it becomes a fire risk. If the dryer has got slow, that's the reason to call.

groups.heading: Commercial
body: Rooftop package units, make-up air, and the heating plant in strata and light industrial buildings. Much of that work sits close to the shop.

feature.title: Boiler repair and replacement in Burnaby — Nation Furnace
feature.description: Boiler service, repair and replacement in Burnaby. Pressure loss, circulation faults and controls, plus straight answers on lifespan and repair versus replace.
feature.lede: Plenty of Burnaby heats with hot water rather than forced air. Radiators in the older houses, in-floor in the newer ones. Boiler work is its own trade, and we do it.
intro: A boiler system is a loop. Water gets heated, a pump pushes it around the house, it gives up its heat at the radiators or the floor, and it comes back. When something goes wrong, the loop is either leaking, not circulating properly, or not getting heated in the first place. Working out which of those you have needs somebody standing in front of it, not a phone description.
feature.caption: Wall-mount boiler with a storage tank, copper manifold, in a Burnaby utility room.
list: Pressure that keeps dropping and needs topping up
No fire, or a burner that lights and drops out
Kettling, banging or a new hum
Leaks at fittings or from the pressure relief valve
Full replacement when the unit is finished
feature.afterList: We also cover boiler repair on our main site's {{link:https://nationheating.ca/boiler-repair-burnaby|Burnaby boiler page}}.

questions.q: What are the most common boiler problems?
a: Pressure that won't stay up, a unit that won't fire or won't hold a flame, some radiators hot while others stay cold, new noise, and leaks at fittings or the relief valve.
All of those are symptoms. Low pressure tells you water is leaving the system; it doesn't tell you where. That's why the first visit is a diagnosis rather than a repair.
questions.schema: Pressure that keeps dropping, a unit that will not fire or will not hold a flame, some radiators hot while others stay cold, new noise, and leaks at fittings or the pressure relief valve. Each of those is a symptom rather than a cause, so the first visit is a diagnosis.

questions.q: How long does a boiler last?
a: That depends more on how it has been looked after than on the badge. Two identical units installed the same year can be in completely different shape a decade later, and the one that got serviced isn't usually the one giving trouble.
For a straight answer on your own boiler we'd want to see the model, the state of the heat exchanger, and what has been done to it since it went in.

A straight answer on a specific boiler means seeing the model, the state of the heat exchanger, and what has been done to it since it went in.

questions.q: Is it worth replacing a 20 year old boiler?
a: Age alone doesn't settle it. Four things do:
bullets: Are parts still available for it?
How does its efficiency compare with a current unit over a full winter?
Is this the first repair, or the third in two years?
after: Discontinued parts or a failed heat exchanger usually mean replacement. A controls fault on an otherwise sound unit usually means repair. We'll tell you which one you've got.
questions.schema: Age alone does not decide it. What matters is whether parts are still available, how its efficiency compares with a current unit over a full heating season, whether the heat exchanger is sound, and whether this is the first repair or the third. Discontinued parts or a failed heat exchanger usually mean replacement.

questions.q: What does a new boiler cost?
a: It comes down to the heat output the house actually needs, the type of boiler, whether the existing venting and gas line suit the new unit, and how much of the current system we can reuse.
Two houses on the same Burnaby street can differ substantially on venting alone. We quote after seeing the house, in writing, with what's included spelled out.
questions.schema: It is set by the heat output the house needs, the type of boiler, whether the existing venting and gas line suit the new unit, and how much of the current system can be reused. Two houses on the same street can differ substantially on venting alone, so the number comes from a site visit.

questions.q: What does a boiler repair cost?
a: A service call, then parts and labour. Nobody can price the parts before the fault is found, so the diagnosis comes first and the repair price follows it.
Two things to ask any company you call: is the service call credited against the repair if you go ahead, and is there a callback charge if the same fault comes back.

areas.title: Nation Furnace service areas — Burnaby, Lower Mainland
areas.description: The Burnaby neighbourhoods we cover across the north, east and south of the city, plus the eleven other Lower Mainland cities we take work in.
areas.lede: We run out of Still Creek Drive and cover Burnaby north, east and south, plus eleven other cities across the Lower Mainland.
intro: The parts of the city are not the same job. Older stock keeps us on radiators and heating that has been rebuilt more than once. Around Metrotown and Brentwood there is a lot of newer building with equipment we fit from scratch. Both keep us busy, in different months.

areas.citiesIntro: Burnaby is home, but the vans get out. Each of these has its own page on our main site.

outro.heading: Not on either list?
body: Call anyway. The boundary is a rough guide rather than a rule, and it costs nothing to ask.

outro.heading: When to book
body: Winter fills up with heating calls and the cooling calls all land in the same week the first real heat does. If what you need is a service rather than a repair, booking it outside those two stretches gets you a better appointment than waiting for something to fail in January.
